nodes.label: notebooks/iTransformer.ipynb
nodes.rationale: The self-contained Kaggle deliverable notebook. This log file is its console stream: every stage, gate, measurement and artifact below was printed by this notebook in one 33,148 s session on 2 x Tesla T4.

nodes.label: Kaggle session console stream
nodes.rationale: 2,148 numbered console lines spanning 3.0 s to 33,148.9 s (~9.2 h). Ends with NbConvert writing 971,567 bytes of executed notebook. This is the evidence base for the study's measured results.

nodes.label: Session runtime environment
nodes.rationale: polars 1.35.2 | torch 2.10.0+cu128 | numpy 2.0.2 on Python 3.12. arch 8.0.0 installed from a pinned offline wheel; polars, pyarrow, numpy, scipy, statsmodels, matplotlib already satisfied. work=/kaggle/working, artifacts=/kaggle/working/artifacts.

nodes.label: Two Tesla T4 devices visible
nodes.rationale: CUDA devices: 2 — cuda:0 Tesla T4 sm_75 and cuda:1 Tesla T4 sm_75. Both were used by the grid, unlike the earlier 894-run session which left one idle for 7.8 h.

nodes.label: bf16 capability gate on sm_75
nodes.rationale: Printed verbatim: 'native bf16: False (is_bf16_supported() says True and is not to be trusted here)'. The gate reads compute capability (sm_75 < 8) rather than torch.cuda.is_bf16_supported(), which defaults to including_emulation=True and would select emulated bf16 slower than fp32.

nodes.label: Parquet discovery on Kaggle
nodes.rationale: Resolved to /kaggle/input/datasets/akmaleyzal/btc1h-raw/BTCUSDT_1h.parquet (6.7 MB) — the three-level web-UI path that the old five-pattern glob could not reach (D71). Discovery succeeded here and the session proceeded.

nodes.label: code_sha256 provenance digest
nodes.rationale: code_sha256 0103dc19fe3450202f32562cce0e16470426af167cce013887e06db8fd1f8936, written into every meta/*.json. Log states the reason: there is no git repository on Kaggle, so the digest is what the traceability contract names the code with — it identifies the code that ran, not the commit someone was standing on with a dirty tree.

nodes.label: 18 in-kernel definition modules
nodes.rationale: modules defined in-kernel: 18 — config.py, __init__.py, segments.py, windows.py, budget.py, features.py, splits.py, model.py, train.py, keff.py, efficiency.py, metrics.py, baselines.py, comparisons.py, economics.py, attention.py, runner.py, report.py. Nothing is on sys.path; the notebook carries the package as definition cells.

nodes.label: Stage 2 — data validation
nodes.rationale: PASSED. bars 75,094 / usable 75,091 / unusable 3; window budget matched docs/ORIGIN_WINDOW_BUDGET.md at all 15 origins by exact equality; feature frame emitted at 75,062 x 12. No relaxation of the segment rule was required.

nodes.label: Three unusable bars, measured
nodes.rationale: Exactly 3 bars, and the same 3 under all three predicates (zero_volume, flat_bar H==L, zero_trades all true): 2019-06-07 21:00 UTC, 2021-02-11 03:00 UTC, 2023-03-24 12:00 UTC. Total unusable is 3, not 9 — the counts are not additive.

nodes.label: Per-origin window budget, exact equality
nodes.rationale: Matched at all 15 origins by exact equality (D45). Training range 13,558 … 15,217 windows on the raw-bar frame; loss_pct falls monotonically from 10.89% (2021-09) to 0.00% (2025-06, 2025-11). Per-block surviving counts range down to 477 of 720 (2020-11 block 6).

nodes.label: Closed-form window count is an upper bound only
nodes.rationale: closed_form_agrees is false at 2020-01, 2020-06, 2021-04, 2021-09 and true at the later origins. Log states: the closed form disagrees wherever a segment is shorter than one window (D51a) and is kept only as an upper bound; windows are counted segment-wise.

nodes.label: Feature frame — 75,062 rows x 12 variates
nodes.rationale: 75,062 rows x 12 variates; dropped 29 rows = one per segment (D52c: r is per segment, so each segment's first bar has no predecessor). Descriptives: r mean 1.9e-5, std 0.007166, min -0.201033, max 0.16028.

nodes.label: K ladder membership as run
nodes.rationale: K=1 [r]; K=4 adds upper_shadow, lower_shadow, log_quote_volume; K=8 adds log_trade_count, taker_buy_ratio, signed_flow, vwap_location; K=12 adds log_parkinson, log_garman_klass, log_rogers_satchell, log_mean_trade_size. Cumulative, exactly one consistent cut.

nodes.label: Rogers-Satchell log floor, 33 bars at kappa
nodes.rationale: log_rogers_satchell: min -20.723, q0.1% -19.805, median -10.909, at-floor 33. The floor is log(kappa) with kappa = 1e-9; RS vanishes on shadowless (marubozu) bars, so 33 of 75,091 usable bars sit exactly on it rather than at -inf.

nodes.label: Stage 3b — effective dimensionality gate
nodes.rationale: GATE DID NOT PASS, and the action was disclosure. Printed: 'DISCLOSE: measured PR at K=8 is 4.393 < 5.0 ... proceed unchanged and disclose the divergence from 5.2's expected K_eff in 4.1b. Do not re-cut the ladder: D01 leaves no second consistent cut over F1-F5.'

nodes.label: Participation ratio per K rung
nodes.rationale: Measured in 35 s. PR_raw 1.000 / 3.327 / 4.269 / 3.984 (sd 0.000 / 0.103 / 0.117 / 0.307); PR_windownorm 1.000 / 3.317 / 4.013 / 3.654; stable_rank 1.000 / 2.355 / 2.701 / 2.173; crosslag_share 0.980 / 0.078 / 0.047 / 0.020. K=12's PR is BELOW K=8's — the 8->12 rung is more redundant than designed. Section 5.2 expected 1 / ~3.5 / ~6.5 / ~7, reasoned and not measured.

nodes.label: corr(K, K_eff) = 0.8280
nodes.rationale: Printed with its reading: 'A reader is entitled to that before reading the K-vs-K_eff horse race: near 1 means the two theories are close to collinear and there is little to separate, whatever the p-value says.' Lower than the ~0.97 anticipated, which makes the horse race more identifiable, not less.

nodes.label: Stage 4 — pre-flight invariants
nodes.rationale: All four plumbing checks passed on cuda:0 before any grid run: use_norm scale invariance, parameter count identical across rungs, single-batch overfit, and the Naive-RW scaler-space mapping per origin.

nodes.label: use_norm scale-invariance check
nodes.rationale: PASSED: 1.42240524 vs 1.42240143, rel = 2.68e-06. The corrected invariant is MSE(c.x)/c^2 == MSE(x), not 'identical loss after x100 scaling' — the target is a channel of the same array so the loss scales by c^2.

nodes.label: 280,472 parameters, identical at every rung
nodes.rationale: Printed 'parameters 280,472 — identical at every rung by construction'. The projection is Linear(d_model -> H), so the count moves with the horizon and not with K; 280,472 is the H=24 figure and is what makes the ladder a fixed-capacity comparison.

nodes.label: Single-batch overfit check
nodes.rationale: single-batch overfit (dropout=0.0): 1.055e-10. Run with dropout disabled deliberately — at the configured 0.1 the loss floors near 7e-2 and a reader following the instruction literally would conclude the plumbing is broken when it is not.

nodes.label: Naive-RW in scaler space, per origin
nodes.rationale: Baseline computed before any model trained. naive_rw_z = -mu_g/sigma_g per origin; mu_g/sigma_g spans -0.00818 … +0.01733 and CHANGES SIGN (negative at 2020-01, 2024-03 among others). sigma_g falls from 0.009151 at 2020-01 to 0.005064 at 2025-01. Log: the tilt is not a constant a reader could subtract, and it tracks the same bull/bear cycle H2 invokes, so it is confounded with the effect of interest.

nodes.label: Stage 5 — RQ1 pilot gate
nodes.rationale: FAILED. 12 pilot runs at origin 1 on its validation sub-block (4 K x 3 seeds, 21-27 s each): validation MSE K=1 0.467551, K=4 0.466160, K=8 0.465441, K=12 0.465767. Run on validation, never on test, so the test blocks stay closed until the design is frozen.

nodes.label: Clark-West pilot statistic, K=1 vs K=8
nodes.rationale: Clark-West K=1 vs K=8 (validation): S* = +0.8759, p = 0.1906 one-sided, T = 1845, h = 24. Clark-West rather than standard DM because the pair is nested and DM is undersized against the alternative the study exists to establish. Does not reject at alpha = 0.05.

nodes.label: Title repositioned to the descriptive variant
nodes.rationale: Printed as a banner: 'FAIL — reposition the title to the descriptive variant NOW, not in week nine (root 8.5)'. The pre-registered action on this exact outcome; it fired before fifteen origins of test blocks were opened, which is the whole reason the gate sits on validation.

nodes.label: Pilot recorded as a selection event
nodes.rationale: Printed: 'Disclose the pilot in section 13.2 as a SELECTION EVENT, stated separately from the DSR trial count — the DSR does not correct for selection over a paper's conclusion.'

nodes.label: 18-probe tuning sweep on origin 1 validation
nodes.rationale: 18 probes over d_model {64,128,256} x e_layers {2,3} x lr {1e-4, 3e-4, 1e-3}, ranked on origin 1 validation MSE. Spread 0.466377 (best) to 0.471792 (worst, d_model 256 / e_layers 2 / lr 1e-4). Ran ~17-24 s per probe, 410.8 s to 768.1 s of session time.

nodes.label: Tuned configuration selected
nodes.rationale: Selected on origin 1 validation: {'d_model': 256, 'e_layers': 3, 'lr': 0.001, 'val_mse': 0.46637744714035684}. The confirmation line echoes only 'TUNED_CONFIG.d_model=256 TUNED_CONFIG.e_layers=3' — the learning rate is absent from the echo, the exact surface where record and run once disagreed (D76).

nodes.label: 1,620-run manifest
nodes.rationale: manifest 1620 unique runs: main 300, uniform 75, fresh 15, horizon 240, ridge 60, dlinear 75, patchtst 75, lstm 75, persist 15, seasonal 15, orthogonal 75, redundant 75, look048 75, look192 75, tuned 75, attention 75, longsched 150, capacity 75. Observed tags in the run stream: itr 528, itrl 150, then 75 each for ptst/lstm/l192/l048/itru/itrt/itrr/itro/itrc/itra/dlin, rdg 60, and 15 each for nsea/npst/itrf.

nodes.label: Resume by glob — 12 complete, 1,608 pending
nodes.rationale: roots searched ['artifacts']; already complete: 12, pending: 1608 — the twelve Stage 5 pilot runs. Log states the rule: completeness is per run_id, both preds/ and meta/ present and meta.status == 'complete'; a run interrupted mid-training leaves no meta so it is redone, losing at most one run (~30 s).

nodes.label: Session budget guard
nodes.rationale: 'prelude took 13 min -> grid gets 10.79 h of the 11.0 h session budget, guard reserves 0.5 h more'. The deadline is stamped at cell 0, not where the guard is constructed, so the prelude (stages 2, 3b, 4, 5 and the tuning sweep) is charged against the session rather than sitting outside it.

nodes.label: Run-level parallelism across both T4s
nodes.rationale: 'devices for the grid: [cuda:0, cuda:1]' then 'run-level parallelism across [cuda:0, cuda:1] (D68)'. One worker thread per visible device off a shared queue; every subsequent run line carries its device tag and completion order interleaves (e.g. [2/1608] on cuda:1 finishes before [1/1608] on cuda:0), which is the queue working. Parallelism at the run level, never the batch level.

nodes.label: Grid execution summary
nodes.rationale: completed 1608, skipped 0, failed 0, remaining 0. wall 8.96 h, mean run 40.1 s, estimated sessions left 0.00; 'remaining after this session: 0 of 1620'. Whole manifest finished inside one session. Per-run wall on the stream ranges ~30 s (K=4, 8-9 epochs) to ~86 s (K=1, 23 epochs); K=1 consistently trains longer than the wider rungs.

nodes.label: Ridge alpha at the edge of its grid
nodes.rationale: The session's only recurring warning, emitted for most of the 60 ridge runs: 'ridge alpha 1e+06 sits at the edge of (0.1 … 1000000.0); the grid may not bracket the optimum'. Validation selection pins alpha at the maximum, i.e. maximal shrinkage — which is why ridge sits closest to the naive baseline rather than beating it.

nodes.label: Panel assembly — 9,675 rows, 2,403 cells
nodes.rationale: 'gathered 1620 runs -> 9675 run-block rows -> 2403 seed-averaged cells'. Every ratio metric is formed from seed-averaged MSEs, never from an average of per-seed ratios. Evaluation is gated on grid completeness; a partial panel is refused rather than reported as a noisier one.

nodes.label: RQ1 — free rung effects
nodes.rationale: MSE 0.862582 / 0.861290 / 0.860653 / 0.861091 at K = 1 / 4 / 8 / 12, SE across origins ~0.0958, n_origins 15 at every rung. R2_oos -0.020455 / -0.018682 / -0.017993 / -0.018570 — every rung negative, so no rung beats Naive-RW. Seed std 0.001334 mean across cells at n=5, reported as a Monte-Carlo diagnostic only. delta MSE 4->8 = +0.000636, 8->12 = -0.000437.

nodes.label: TOST equivalence test on the 8->12 rung
nodes.rationale: mean delta = -0.000437, margin = +/-0.000159 (0.25 x delta(4->8), fixed in advance), p = (0.9734, 0.0002), G = 15 -> NOT shown equivalent. Log states the reason the margin is pre-registered: a non-significant delta is a failure to reject, not evidence of equivalence, and choosing the margin after seeing the rung is p-hacking.

nodes.label: Davidson-MacKinnon J-test, K vs K_eff
nodes.rationale: K augmented by K_eff: t = +3.293, p = 0.0011 (the K explanation is rejected). K_eff augmented by K: t = -0.348, p = 0.7281 (the K_eff explanation is not). Non-nested comparison, because K and K_eff are competing explanations rather than nested ones. H1 survives its own horse race on a ladder where every rung has negative skill.

nodes.label: RQ2 — decay slope beta1
nodes.rationale: beta1 = +0.000256, t = +0.717, G = 15, N = 90. Wild cluster restricted bootstrap one-sided p (H1: beta1 < 0): Rademacher 0.7381, Webb 0.7346 -> headline 0.7381. Not supported and the sign is wrong. A(i,b) panel shows per-block values from -0.004502 to +0.007932. Log adds: effective independence is bounded near 4 by training-window overlap, well below G = 15.

nodes.label: Minimum detectable beta1
nodes.rationale: MDE at 80% power, alpha = 0.05: -0.000920. Observed +0.000256 is INSIDE (undetectable) it, so RQ2 is reported as descriptive. Log states the pre-registered reason: a non-significant beta1 is otherwise indistinguishable from a design that could never have detected decay.

nodes.label: Training-disjoint re-estimate, five triples at G=3
nodes.rationale: Training-window overlap 79.2% at stride 1, 58.3% at 2, 37.5% at 3, 16.7% at 4; disjoint only at stride 5, leaving G=3. The five triples: [2020-01, 2022-02, 2024-03] +0.001250 p=0.8732; [2020-06, 2022-07, 2024-08] -0.000449 p=0.0761; [2020-11, 2022-12, 2025-01] -0.000218 p=0.3786; [2021-04, 2023-05, 2025-06] +0.001625 p=0.9322; [2021-09, 2023-10, 2025-11] -0.000926 p=0.1256. Log: at G=3 these will very likely be inconclusive, and THAT IS THE FINDING — it bounds what the full-panel p-value can honestly claim.

nodes.label: A_attn — uniform-attention control
nodes.rationale: beta1 = -0.000006, t = -0.438, G = 15, N = 90; WCR one-sided p Rademacher 0.3380 / Webb 0.3387 -> headline 0.3387. Attention neither decays nor helps. Separates the information story from the capacity story, at runs Figure 5 needs anyway.

nodes.label: Falsification arm — aged minus fresh
nodes.rationale: As printed: mean(aged - fresh) = -0.053341 over 45 (origin, block) cells — a scaler-space MSE figure and therefore NOT interpretable as written, since the two arms are fitted 90 days apart and carry different sigma_g (~99.7% of it is scaler drift and the sign reads backwards). The scale-free restatement is RelMSE +0.000828. Log's own reading: positive means the fresh model really is better, so decay is age; near zero while beta1 < 0 means beta1 is calendar, not age.

nodes.label: RQ3 — decay estimand undefined
nodes.rationale: decay_panel returns shape (0, 7) — zero rows. All 15 origins EXCLUDED by name on mean R2_oos <= 0 ('2020-01' … '2025-11'), never silently dropped. RQ3 RETURNS NO ANSWER and that is the finding: D(i,b) is a proportion of skill lost and there is no skill to lose a proportion of. Required wording: 'the decay estimand is undefined under non-positive out-of-sample skill' — never 'no decay detected within 180 days', which is right-censored phrasing that asserts an edge the data does not contain.

nodes.label: tau sensitivity — undefined at all four thresholds
nodes.rationale: tau = 2.5% / 5.0% (HEADLINE) / 10.0% / 50.0% all return 'UNDEFINED — no origin has positive mean skill'. Thresholds pre-registered before the curve was seen, so the null is not a post-hoc choice.

nodes.label: Log-rank test unavailable, H3 untestable
nodes.rationale: 'log-rank K=8 vs K=1 UNAVAILABLE: surviving origins K=8 0, K=1 0.' H3 compares decay RATES, so it needs an edge in both arms; with none, H3 is untestable rather than rejected.

nodes.label: paper_numbers.json written
nodes.rationale: Two copies written in the same session: 'wrote artifacts/paper_numbers.json' (the grid's immutable evidence copy) and 'wrote /kaggle/working/paper/paper_numbers.json' (the manuscript source). Every table and figure is generated from that file rather than transcribed.

nodes.label: Six panel parquets
nodes.rationale: amplification_panel.parquet 0.00 MB, decay_panel.parquet 0.00 MB (zero rows by the exclusion guard), keff_table.parquet 0.01 MB, naive_rw_by_origin.parquet 0.00 MB, run_block_metrics.parquet 0.14 MB, seed_averaged_cells.parquet 0.05 MB.

nodes.label: Persisted predictions and metadata
nodes.rationale: 'preds 1620 files | meta 1621 files' — one meta per run plus tuning_selection.json. remaining runs: 0. Closing instruction: 'Save Version now, then attach this output as the next session's input Dataset. Nothing else needs doing by hand.' Raw predictions are persisted because DM tests, per-regime analysis and the economics all need them.

nodes.label: Report generation pass
nodes.rationale: report: 1620 completed runs under artifacts; 9675 run-block rows -> 2403 seed-averaged cells; 36 architecture cells; efficiency 16 spans, rolling 3044 windows; 66 pairs, MCS over 12 models; 225 economic cells, 52120 equity points; DA over 300 runs. The 66-pair / 12-model matrix and the 225 economic cells are the pre-D74/D77 widths, before the LSTM and the two naive comparators were admitted.

nodes.label: Nine LaTeX tables rendered
nodes.rationale: table1_dataset, table2_efficiency, table2b_keff, table3_architecture, table4_main, table5_decay, table6_dm, table7_horizons, table8_economics. No table9 — the exploratory-arms table that the disclosure rules require in its own table did not yet exist at this vintage.

nodes.label: Six figures rendered
nodes.rationale: figure2b_rolling, figure3_decay, figure4_relmse, figure5_attention, figure6_horizons, figure7_equity, each as .pdf and .png; panels written to /kaggle/working/paper/panels. Figures 1 and 2 are absent from the listing — at this vintage they were marked 'drawn by hand' and therefore did not exist.

nodes.label: Robustness arm status board
nodes.rationale: longsched run, capacity run, attention run. Printed with the commitment: 'An arm reading not run is a pre-registered exploratory arm awaiting its runs, not a failure. Whatever it returns goes in the paper: an arm reported only when it agrees with the headline is not a robustness arm.'

nodes.label: NbConvert export of the executed notebook
nodes.rationale: Session closes by converting __notebook__.ipynb to notebook (971,567 bytes written) and then to html, preceded by two harmless SyntaxWarnings from mistune and nbconvert's filter_links. This export is the copy carrying every output — and the one file that must never be committed over the generated notebook.
